name: Zhevra Hooves
summary: Across the Barrens, zhevras graze in the open savannah. Their hooves prove a hunter can face swift, powerful prey.

sections.title: Trophies of the Hunt
sections.body: Zhevras graze across the Barrens, but their compact, muscular legs can strike hard. Sergra Darkthorn, the orc shaman in charge of the Crossroads, sends aspiring Horde scouts to gather hooves from zhevra runners. The hunt sharpens a fledgling hunter's instincts and resilience. A panicked runner can kick even a sturdy tauren flat. Intact hooves show a hunter can handle swift, kicking quarry before taking on Kalimdor's deadliest predators.

faq.answer: Sergra Darkthorn, an orc shaman at the Crossroads in the Barrens, asks hunters to bring her four Zhevra Hooves to prove they are ready for tougher game.

faq.q: Where do Zhevra Hooves come from?
faq.answer: Zhevra Hooves come from zhevra runners grazing across the open savannah north and south of the Crossroads.

faq.q: Why are zhevra dangerous to hunt?
faq.answer: Zhevras can strike with great force using their hind legs. A sprinting zhevra can kick an adult tauren off their feet, though zhevras are less aggressive than raptors or prowlers.

faq.q: Why does Sergra have hunters track zhevra rather than fiercer beasts?
faq.answer: Sergra sees zhevras as a step up from plainstriders. They give newcomers firm but safe practice before they face truly lethal creatures.

angles.text: As a new Horde recruit arriving in the Barrens, you can prove your fitness to defend the Crossroads by harvesting hooves for Sergra Darkthorn.
As a hunter, tracking zhevras across the savannah teaches you to handle swift herd animals that can turn and strike with powerful kicks.
